pr_title: Reduce the number of expensive calls in the Windows stats queries for dockershim
pr_body:

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This improves the response time and minimizes the calls to the system stats which reduces overall cpu for kubelet.  This is done by passing the container object, which has the information required, instead of querying for it on every container via the dockerservice. It also caches some information like the runtime info so it is not queried on every container.

Dockershim create a  new namepiped instance to docker every call causing reads and higher cpu usage.  (Containerd re-uses the same namedpipe instance so doesn't see the same cpu spike).


#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
<!--

-->
Fixes #104283 
#### Special notes for your reviewer:

I initially included the commits from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105744 but moved it to a separate PR.  That PR also improves the overall CPU used here but not opening and list all the containers twice.

> For the second question, I think that if we know we want to backport this fix it might be better to try and limit it to Windows only (Unless there are issues on Linux similar to what I mentioned above) just to limit the scope.
> I'm curious what @SergeyKanzhelev thinks here.

Looking briefly into it feels strange that `info` is only seems to be used for the `info.DockerRootDir`, so practically this value can be cached for much longer. I wonder what's the size of `info` if we only use a single field, it looks like a big waste. 

If you can look a bit on savings we get on Linux - it may help to say whether we need it. The only concern with cache is the data consistency, that docker will be reinstalled in those 60 seconds... but I doubt it is a big deal.

Also, please correct the release notes if you will proceed with the fix for Linux as well.

> Looking briefly into it feels strange that `info` is only seems to be used for the `info.DockerRootDir`, so practically this value can be cached for much longer. I wonder what's the size of `info` if we only use a single field, it looks like a big waste.

I had a similar thoughts for only that field but was being conservative on the timing.  When you say it looks like a big waste do you mean caching the object in memory or the query? If we cached just the string would be better?

> The only concern with cache is the data consistency, that docker will be reinstalled in those 60 seconds... but I doubt it is a big deal.

Is re-installing docker or restarting it while kubelet is running a supported scenario?


> If you can look a bit on savings we get on Linux - it may help to say whether we need it. 

There isn't much savings from Linux side communication across the pipe fast (I will double check this). This why I didn't remove all those calls from linux. The issue on the windows is that it creates a new instance of a named pipe per call to docker. When we make 4 calls to docker over the pipe per container every 10 seconds (calls from eviction manager) it causes quite a bit of I/O. Plus there can be scrapes from other things interested in metrics (metric server and other third part metric tools) which can cause the [response be over 1m 20s ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104283#issue-965577389) even though it was successful.  We don't see this type of latency on Linux.

>limit it to Windows only (Unless there are issues on Linux similar to what I mentioned above) just to limit the scope.

The reason it touched both is because the the function `getContainerStats` that is shared across version `_windows.go` and `_linux.go` needs to take the container not just the id of the container to limit the calls on the windows side.

Since its not expensive on linux those calls don't matter as much and are duplicated but on windows it causes more I/O.  For example we have all the labels/metadata/annotations  about the all the containers from this single call

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/27d3a9ec57e88567b5a5aebbf59cd1b72e01937c/pkg/kubelet/dockershim/docker_stats.go#L51

but we get it again here for _every_ container even though we already have it

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/27d3a9ec57e88567b5a5aebbf59cd1b72e01937c/pkg/kubelet/dockershim/docker_stats_windows.go#L75

> > The only concern with cache is the data consistency, that docker will be reinstalled in those 60 seconds... but I doubt it is a big deal.
>

It really depends on what data from `info` is used. I'm saying re-install because assuming that just the root dir is used. But if more is used, simple process crash may lead for inconsistency. If for sure we only using DockerRootDir, maybe we can just store it as a constant fir the duration of kubelet lifecycle. No need to even refresh.

>

This will be mostly CPU consumed than, rather than real delays. Still a valuable save. With the dockershim gone soon, may not worth your effort checking it.

From a latency perspective on a for these improvements for windows, the more happening on the node (ie. if there are pods being created/deleted) the slower the response is.  The value goes up with the number of containers, or concurrent calls as well. 

With a stable cluster (no pods created/deleted) there is a noticeable difference ~480ms to ~280ms. 3 calls to the stats endpoint is chosen as that was number of calls in the initial report (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/104283).  The difference is dramatic as the number of calls to the endpoint increases (5 concurrent is ~1s vs 450ms)  but is a bit unrealistic in reality, though it simulates multiple calls to the docker pipe during container creation.

```
go run . -l 3 -n capz-conf-n4466 -s 0 
Starting 0 containers on node capz-conf-n4466
pods at start: 14
starting 0 containers
run call to stats 3 times
timing: capz-conf-n4466/proxy/stats/summary?only_cpu_and_memory=true took 480.129248ms
timing: capz-conf-n4466/proxy/stats/summary?only_cpu_and_memory=true took 498.438276ms
timing: capz-conf-n4466/proxy/stats/summary?only_cpu_and_memory=true took 498.858143ms
pods at end: 14
```

After the fix:
```
go run . -l 3 -n capz-conf-n4466 -s 0 
Starting 0 containers on node capz-conf-n4466
pods at start: 14
starting 0 containers
run call to stats 3 times
timing: capz-conf-n4466/proxy/stats/summary?only_cpu_and_memory=true took 265.476383ms
timing: capz-conf-n4466/proxy/stats/summary?only_cpu_and_memory=true took 280.700123ms
timing: capz-conf-n4466/proxy/stats/summary?only_cpu_and_memory=true took 297.86408ms
pods at end: 14
```

> 
> > > The only concern with cache is the data consistency, that docker will be reinstalled in those 60 seconds... but I doubt it is a big deal.
> > 

Hm, reinstalling docker... Generally, Kubelet and Docker are registered as Services, and Kubelet is set as dependent on Docker. In this scenario, if you'd want to reinstall docker, you'd have to stop the service first, which you can't without stopping Kubelet first, unless forcefully stopping Docker, which automatically stops Kubelet as well. Afterwards, both services will have to be restarted, so this shouldn't be a problem in most cases.

This change is pretty straight-forward, IMO. It shouldn't cause any problems, and it is limited to just Windows Docker.
/assign @derekwaynecarr

issue_context.title: Context Deadline exceeded when Metrics Server calls Windows Stats endpoint
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

Metric server reports "context Deadline exceeded when calling metrics endpoint.  This cause its with `kubectl top pods` and potentially HPA if it is being used.

```
E0726 23:44:07.782895       1 manager.go:111] unable to fully collect metrics: unable to fully scrape metrics from source kubelet_summary:aksnpwin000002: unable to fetch metrics from Kubelet aksnpwin000002 (10.240.0.97): Get https://10.240.0.97:10250/stats/summary?only_cpu_and_memory=true: context deadline exceeded
```

Looking at kubelet logs this with `-v5` we can see the request is return in time but is over the 60sec timeout the metric server defaults.  

```
sls -Path .\kubelet.err* -Pattern "latency=""\d+m\d+.\d+s"""       
kubelet.err-20210727T134827.473.log:9418:I0727 13:13:23.610822     984 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="GET" URI="/stats/summary?only_cpu_and_memory=true" latency="1m9.8193246s"  
```


When I am able to reproduce this I can see several components querying the stats endpoint at once including sometimes an internal error timeout.


```
kubelet.err-20210727T134827.473.log:9333:I0727 13:13:14.034332     984 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="GET" URI="/stats/summary?only_cpu_and_memory=true" latency="2m0.2529876s"
userAgent="Go-http-client/2.0" srcIP="10.240.0.15:35654" resp=500 statusStack="\ngoroutine 2624574 ....
kubelet.err-20210727T134827.473.log:9418:I0727 13:13:23.610822     984 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="GET" URI="/stats/summary?only_cpu_and_memory=true" latency="1m9.8193246s"
userAgent="Go-http-client/2.0" srcIP="10.240.0.15:35654" resp=200
kubelet.err-20210727T134827.473.log:9483:I0727 13:13:24.289825     984 httplog.go:89] "HTTP" verb="GET" URI="/stats/summary" latency="1m21.3725636s" userAgent="Ruby" srcIP="10.240.0.29:48702"
resp=200
```

#### What you expected to happen:

Gathering stats for windows to not timeout

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

It is difficult to reproduce. I've written a little program that manually does multiple calls windows stats system call and i can reproduce it.
